_readme: Story text for the screens. Writers can change any sentence. Do not change the names on the left side of the colons (the keys), or the game cannot find the text.

lines: A rocket waits on the launch pad. Something is about to go very wrong.

name_screen.title: First things first. What is your name?

destination_screen.title: Where are we going?
destination_screen.coming_soon_line: Coming soon! This kind of trip is not built yet.

mission_screen.title: What is the mission for?
mission_screen.goal_heading: The mission is a success if:

build_screen.title: Build your spacecraft. Pick one of each.
build_screen.far_note: Far from Mars: solar panels make {sun}% of their Mars power and antennas send data at {far}% of their Mars speed.

review_screen.title: Before launch: does it all add up?

ship._readme: Names on the ship. room_names = the sign above each room's doorway (left side of the colon must match the room names in game_data.json). future_stations = the floating label over each glowing floor marker. flight_stations = the label over the Science and Comms markers during Flight (they only work in Mars orbit).

flight_stations.capture: Science station: works in Mars orbit
flight_stations.downlink: Comms station: works in Mars orbit

walk_screen.controls_hint: WASD = walk    Space = jump    Mouse = look    E = use    Tab = raise arm (dashboard)    Esc = free the mouse

scientist.name: The Scientist
scientist.description: You know spacecraft, orbits and Mars better than anyone in the room. The general just needs you to decide.

janitor.name: The Janitor
janitor.description: You know every room in this building. You know nothing about spacecraft.

student.name: The Student
student.description: You came on a school tour and took a wrong turn. You know a little from class. The general points at you anyway.

mars_orbit.name: Mars orbit
mars_orbit.description: Circle Mars and map it from above.

europa_flyby.name: Europa (Jupiter)
europa_flyby.description: Fly past an icy moon. No crew, no landing.

launch_vehicles._readme: Plain names on purpose: the numbers are made up for now, so we do not use real rocket names.

small.name: Small rocket
small.description: The cheapest. But it has the most launch moments, and the timing is tight.

medium.name: Medium rocket
medium.description: A middle price, with a middle number of launch moments and normal timing.

large.name: Large rocket
large.description: The most expensive. But it has the fewest launch moments, and the timing is forgiving.

mars_ice.name: Map the ice on Mars
mars_ice.description: Send a spacecraft to orbit Mars and take pictures to find where the ice is. Future astronauts will need that water.

goal_rules._readme: One sentence for each goal rule. {value} and {unit} are filled in from the mission limits in game_data.json.

crew_supplies._readme: The Crew supplies group on the arm dashboard (shown in Flight and Arrival only). names and units = the words on each row. of_word = the words between the amount left and the full size, for example "1250 kg of 1300".
crew_supplies.title: Crew supplies

flight._readme: Words on the screen during Flight (Stage 3): the Life Support stations. prompts = the line shown near a station (after "Press E:"); the _done and _none lines show when there is nothing left to do. ration_panel = the Food station's little screen. Batch 9: three legs. event_banners = the red banner while an event pours out a supply. leg_line = which leg it is. task_names = the names used when a skipped task is mentioned.

prompts.air: Air station: run the oxygen generator
prompts.air_done: Air station: the oxygen generator is running
prompts.air_event: Air station: fix the air leak
prompts.water_filter_done: Water station: the filter is changed
prompts.harvest_done: Food station: the garden is harvested
prompts.nothing: Nothing to do here right now

ration_panel.title: FOOD STATION
ration_panel.body: Rationing means the crew eats a little less each day, so the food lasts longer. Once it is on, it stays on.

event_banners.water_leak: WATER LEAK! Go to the Water station
event_banners.air_leak: AIR LEAK! Go to the Air station
event_banners.food_spoil: FOOD SPOILING! Go to the Food station

timed_press_test._readme: Words for the timed-press test bench (scenes/timed_press_test.tscn).
timed_press_test.title: Timed press test
timed_press_test.label: PRESS NOW
timed_press_test.hint: Press {key} (or click) when the ring closes on the target.

launch_screen._readme: Words for the Launch screen (Stage 2). moments = the names of the launch moments. cost_kinds = how a Miss cost is written ({amount} is a percent).
launch_screen.title: Launch!
launch_screen.hint: Press SPACE (or click) when the ring closes on the target.

cost_kinds.distance: landed {amount}% of the way off the target

cutscene_intro._readme: Words for the intro cutscene in scenes/cutscene_intro.tscn.

subtitles._readme: The subtitle lines at the bottom of the cutscene. Each line has a speaker name (shown in amber) and the words (shown in white). The AnimationPlayer calls show_subtitle with one of these names at the right time.

general_who.speaker: General
general_who.text: This mission launches on schedule. Who will run it?

orbit_burn_screen._readme: Words for the Orbit burn screen (Stage 4, before the walk). The cost text uses launch_screen.cost_kinds ({amount} is a percent).
orbit_burn_screen.title: Orbit burn
orbit_burn_screen.hint: Press E (or click) when the ring closes on the target.
orbit_burn_screen.no_loss: No losses. We are in orbit!

science._readme: Words for the science pass (Stage 4, in the walk). banner_* = the calm banner at the top while a window is open ({seconds} = seconds left). station_* = the floating label over the glowing floor marker (open = while its window is open). prompts = the line after the Press E hint. sent_home = result line ({gb} = gigabits).
science.banner_capture: TARGET IN VIEW: Science bay, press E ({seconds})
science.banner_downlink: GROUND STATION IN VIEW: Comms room, press E ({seconds})

prompts.capture_wait: Science station: the target is not in view
prompts.downlink: Comms station: send the data home
prompts.downlink_wait: Comms station: the ground station is not in view

report_screen._readme: Words for the mission report: the three buttons (retry = go back to the newest checkpoint from before the first failure; same_design = keep your parts, pick a destination again; start_fresh = forget everything, start with your name), the finding cause line, and the log section. cause_overrides = a finding that has its own cause sentence instead of a list of parts.
report_screen.no_checkpoint_tip: There is no checkpoint saved yet.
report_screen.red_build_tip: Your build was already over a limit at launch, so a retry would fail again. Use Same design / new destination to change the parts, or Start fresh.

cause_overrides.power_event: Your parts decided how much power you had to cut. The failure came from not rerouting power in time.

report_screen.no_stage1_choice: none. This came from what happened in Flight and Arrival.
report_screen.no_costs: No damage from any missed press!
report_screen.crew_damage_line: Crew harmed because a supply ran out: {amount}%
report_screen.science_left_line: Still on the ship, never sent: {gb} Gb
report_screen.science_note: For your information. It does not change MISSION SUCCESS yet.
report_screen.surface_placeholder: This destination is a surface site. The work on the surface is not built yet, so this report ends right after the landing.
report_screen.flyby_placeholder: This destination is a flyby. The flyby itself is not built yet, so this report ends right after the trip.
report_screen.surface_power_line: Power spare at the end: {w} W

destination_materials._readme: Names of the things a surface site has (the ids are in data/destinations.json, materials).

landing_screen._readme: Words for the Landing screen (Stage 4, surface destinations). The cost text uses launch_screen.cost_kinds ({amount} is a percent).
landing_screen.title: Landing!
landing_screen.hint: Press SPACE (or click) when the ring closes on the target.
landing_screen.no_losses: No losses. A soft landing right on the target!

arrival_goals._readme: Words for the mission goal when the trip is NOT Mars orbit (the numbers are in data/events.json: surface_work, flyby_pass; {gb} is the planned data in Gb). name and description replace the Mars orbit mission card on the mission screen and the name on the report. rules = the checklist lines. {gb} is the planned data in Gb.

surface.name: Collect a sample and send data home
surface.description: Land, walk out, collect one sample, run the instrument and send the data home. The days on the surface are limited by your power and your crew supplies.

rules.sample: Collect the sample before the days run out
rules.data_sent: Send home at least {gb} Gb of data
rules.power_ok: Keep power out of the red
rules.supplies_ok: Keep food, water and air out of the red

flyby.name: Fly past Europa
flyby.description: Fly past the icy moon and send home what you saw. Radio takes a long time, so every command goes out early.

rules.data_sent: Send home at least {gb} Gb of data

surface_screen._readme: Words for the surface area (Stage 4, surface destinations). {material} is a name from destination_materials. Batch 9: three tasks. next_task = the banner at the top shows the next task to do.
surface_screen.controls_hint: WASD = walk    Space = jump    Mouse = look    E = use    Esc = free the mouse
surface_screen.banner_start: Collect the {material} sample before the days run out!

prompts.send: Press E: Send the data home

next_task.send: Next: send the data home from the lander

surface_screen.banner_all_done: All three tasks done! Well done.

flyby_screen._readme: Words for the Europa flyby (Stage 4, flyby destinations). The player stands in mission control and cannot walk, so Space is the key.
flyby_screen.title: Europa flyby: mission control
flyby_screen.hint: You are in mission control (you cannot walk). Press SPACE or click when the ring closes.
flyby_screen.delay_note: Every command arrives that much later, so send early!
flyby_screen.caption: SEND: {moment}
flyby_screen.pass_line: Closest approach! The commands are arriving...
flyby_screen.sent_line: Sent home: {gb} Gb of the {planned} Gb planned

part_trade_offs._readme: One plain-English trade-off line for every part version (shown when you point at its button on the Build screen). The ids are the slot and version ids from game_data.json parts.

solar_panel.small: Cheap and light, but it makes the least power.
solar_panel.medium: A middle choice for power, cost and weight.
solar_panel.large: Lots of power, but heavy and costly.
solar_panel.rtg: Makes power from heat, so weak sunlight does not matter. Heavy and costly.

battery.light: Cheaper and lighter, but gives less power in the shadow pass.
battery.standard: The normal batteries that are already on the ship.
battery.large: More power in the shadow pass, but heavier and costs more.

camera.basic: Light and cheap, but it collects little data.
camera.high_res: Collects lots of data, but heavy and costly. It needs a fast antenna.

antenna.small: Light and cheap, but slow, so less data gets home.

computer.compact: Lighter and cheaper, but it stores less data.
computer.standard: The normal computer that is already on the ship.
computer.big_memory: Stores more data before you must send it home, but costs more and uses more power.

thermal.standard: The normal heater and blankets that are already on the ship.
thermal.insulated: The heater uses less power and the cold hurts less, but it is heavier and costs more.

propulsion.standard: The normal engine that is already on the ship.
propulsion.efficient: A missed launch or burn press loses half as much fuel, but it is heavier and costs more.

life_support.standard: The normal air, water and food systems that are already on the ship.
life_support.garden: Grow food in flight, but it is heavy, costs more and uses power.
life_support.recycler: The crew uses less water, but it is heavy, costs more and uses power.

heat_shield.basic: Cheap, but a missed press can hurt the landing.
heat_shield.strong: Heavier and costs more, but a missed press costs half as much.

parachute.basic: Cheap, but a missed press can hurt the landing.
parachute.strong: Heavier and costs more, but a missed press costs half as much.

landing_system.basic: Cheap, but a missed press can hurt the landing.
landing_system.strong: Heavier and costs more, but a missed press costs half as much.

surface_tools.scoop: The simple tool that is already on the lander.
surface_tools.drill: A sample try uses half the power, but it is heavy and costs more.
surface_tools.lab: The instrument collects more data, but it weighs more, costs more and uses power.

radiation_shield.none: No weight and no cost, but radiation destroys data.
radiation_shield.vault: Stops most of the radiation, but heavy and costly.
